parsed.basis: Augšdaugavas novads in eastern Latgale, around Daugavpils, inherits Latvia's national framework: same-sex conduct is not criminalised and there is no trans-specific offence, while residents lack a dedicated legal gender recognition statute and documented gender-identity anti-discrimination protection. Hate-crime enforcement is the main gap, including attacks in Daugavpils where police closed the investigation and the Prosecutor General ordered it reopened, and a 2024 European Court ruling that Latvia failed to prosecute a homophobic attack. The novads is largely rural and socially more conservative than Riga, with limited tourism and trans-specific support, so an outed visitor would face greater local hostility and less reliable first-instance police help, though national prosecutors and courts can intervene and imprisonment is not a documented outcome.
